w10_T4_002190: A craft supplier had 32 boxes of beads in the stockroom, and a second delivery raised the count to 2 times that number. A returned order then added 42 more boxes to the same shelf. Every box holds 7 bags of beads, and a courier brought 71 loose bags to go with them. Each bag contains 7 beads. The stockroom is 25 metres long, and the supplier quotes its dispatch times in minutes rather than hours. How many beads are in the stockroom?
w10_T4_002194: On Thursday morning a bakery split 201 sacks of flour equally between its 3 kitchens. Before lunch a mill delivered 12 more sacks to the first kitchen. Every sack in that kitchen makes 9 loaves. In the evening a partner bakery sent 55 finished loaves across to the same kitchen. How many loaves does the first kitchen have?
w10_T4_002197: A camp had 109 packets of soup and used 99 of them during the first week. Every packet still in the cupboard makes 8 bowls. A parent donated 38 ready-made bowls of soup for the weekend. The hikers ate 74 bowls on Saturday. A late delivery added 3 more bowls that evening. The camp sleeps 60 people. How many bowls of soup are there now?
w10_T4_002200: A depot loaded 80 crates onto each of 9 lorries. The crates were then shared equally between 6 regional stores, and the northern store took the first share. That store sold 63 crates in a fortnight. Every crate still there holds 5 boxes of soap. A supermarket bought 280 boxes from the northern store, and a returned pallet brought 43 boxes back to it. The depot has run this route for a dozen years. How many boxes does the northern store have?
w10_T4_002203: A cinema had 155 boxes of popcorn ready on Friday morning and sold 52 of them before noon. At lunchtime a delivery added 50 boxes to the counter. During the afternoon the kitchen made another 16, and in the early evening a supplier sent 36 more. Every box on the counter is filled from 4 scoops of popcorn. The cinema lists its film lengths in minutes rather than hours. How many scoops are needed for the boxes on the counter?
w10_T4_002213: A print shop bound 141 folders, and each folder holds 9 booklets. Every booklet contains 6 pages. The pages were then shared equally between 6 archive boxes, and the first archive box took one share. That box's pages were later split equally between 3 shelves, with the top shelf taking the first part. The counter is 4 metres long, the shop has been open for a dozen years, and it quotes its jobs in minutes rather than hours. How many pages are on the top shelf?
w10_T4_002219: On Monday morning a wholesaler had 176 sacks of coffee and sold 36 of them straight away. By the afternoon a bulk order had doubled the number of sacks in the store. In the evening a second order doubled that number again. The next morning the sacks were shared equally between 4 roasteries, and the first roastery took its share. Every sack at that roastery fills 3 barrels of roasted beans. How many barrels does the first roastery fill?
w10_T4_002221: Ana counted 225 tiles in the yard and found 7 more behind the shed. Her brother Luis, who had bought fewer tiles than Ana, added 38 from his own load. The tiles were then shared equally between 5 rooms, and the kitchen took the first share. Every tile in the kitchen is cut into 4 pieces for the mosaic. Then 44 of those pieces cracked and were thrown away. Ana prices her work in cents rather than dollars. How many mosaic pieces does the kitchen have?
w10_T4_002225: On Saturday morning a fishmonger had 112 boxes of ice, and each box holds 4 blocks. Before lunch a supplier delivered 30 loose blocks. In the afternoon a partner shop sent 53 more blocks across the road. Through the evening 71 blocks melted away in the warm weather. The shop front is 7 metres wide, and its opening times are written in minutes past the hour rather than in hours. How many blocks of ice are left?
w10_T4_002236: On Sunday morning a hostel had 62 clean sheets and sent 14 of them away to be mended. The rest were divided equally between 2 floors. During the afternoon the laundry delivered 40 sheets to the ground floor. In the early evening a hotel lent that floor 17 more. Later that night 4 of the ground floor's sheets were ruined by a leaking radiator. How many sheets does the ground floor have?
w10_T4_002240: Yasmin bottled 206 litres of apple juice on each of 3 days. A supermarket order then took 297 litres from the store. Her partner Callum, who bottled far less than Yasmin, took another 213 litres for his own shop. A school fete bought 97 litres after that. The pair have pressed apples together for a dozen years. How many litres are left in the store?
w10_T4_002241: Ravi had 210 planks in the workshop and used 176 of them on a decking job. A merchant delivered 80 more planks the next day. His colleague Signe, who had fewer planks than Ravi, passed him 45 from her own stock. A neighbour then bought 50 planks from him. Every plank still in the workshop can be cut into 4 shelf boards. The workshop stands 90 metres from the main road. How many shelf boards could Ravi cut?
w10_T4_002242: A charity had 97 blankets in its store and bought 50 more at a clearance sale. It sent 33 blankets to a shelter the same week. A matching donation then raised its blanket count to 2 times that number. Every blanket in the store is packed with 6 clothes pegs for the washing line. A volunteer later lost 112 pegs when a bag split. The store opens 5 days a week, and its rota is written in minutes rather than hours. How many pegs does the charity have?
w10_T4_002245: On Monday morning a factory had 225 reels of thread and used 199 of them on a big order. Every reel still in the store holds 8 spools. During the afternoon a supplier delivered 53 loose spools of the same kind. In the evening the staff worked out that each spool carries 5 metres of thread. A repair job then used 715 metres from the store. How many metres of thread are left?
w10_T4_002246: A wholesaler had 193 cartons and returned 32 of them as damaged. Every carton still in the store holds 3 boxes. Each box contains 9 sachets of spice. A supplier added 15 loose sachets to the same shelf. All of the sachets were then shared equally between 6 shops, and the market shop took the first share. The wholesaler's van covers 140 kilometres on its round. How many sachets went to the market shop?
w10_T4_002248: A gardener had 16 packets of bulbs and planted 12 of them along the path. Then 2 packets were spoiled when the shed flooded. Every packet still dry holds 7 bulbs. A neighbour gave her 48 loose bulbs, and the garden centre added 7 more. Squirrels then dug up and destroyed 14 bulbs. The path itself is 22 metres long. How many bulbs does the gardener have?
w10_T4_002251: A running club's charity fund stood at 210 pounds at the start of the month. A bake sale added 39 pounds and a car wash brought in 23. A member's sponsored run raised 43 pounds, and a quiz night added 40 more. A local firm then donated 78 pounds to the same fund. A collection tin in the clubhouse held a final 10 pounds. The club has a dozen junior members and 85 seniors. How many pounds are in the fund now?
w10_T4_002254: A depot had 209 crates of oranges and took in 20 more from the docks. A supermarket bought 178 crates the same morning. Every crate still in the depot holds 4 nets of oranges. The nets were then shared equally between 3 market stalls, and the first stall took its share. The depot prices its fruit in cents rather than dollars. How many nets went to the first stall?
w10_T4_002257: On Tuesday morning a dairy had 98 churns and a neighbouring farm sent 28 more. Every churn holds 5 litres of milk. At midday the milk was shared equally between 3 bottling lines, and the first line took its share. During the afternoon a tanker added 74 litres to that line. In the evening a small farm delivered another 40 litres to the same line. The dairy keeps a dozen cows of its own and employs 46 staff. How many litres has the first line received?
w10_T4_002268: A bookbinder had 221 reams in the store and bought 64 more at auction. A college order then used up 77 reams. Every ream still in the store is cut into 8 blocks. Each block is folded into 3 signatures, and every signature carries 5 printed pages. The bindery has worked on this street for a dozen years. How many printed pages could the store's paper make?
w10_T4_002278: A kennel had 92 bags of dog food in the store. A busy boarding week used 70 of them. Then 10 bags went to the rescue centre down the road. A mouse spoiled 5 more bags, and 3 were given to a volunteer for her own dogs. A supplier delivered 3 replacement bags that afternoon. The kennel has room for 24 dogs and writes its feeding times in minutes rather than hours. How many bags of dog food are in the store?
w10_T4_002280: A choir had 72 music folders and sent 16 of them away to be rebound. Half of the folders that remained went to the tenors and half to the basses. The tenors were then given 23 more folders by a retiring member. A neighbouring choir lent them another 19, and the librarian found 11 in the vestry cupboard. How many folders do the tenors have now?
w10_T4_002281: A packing plant had 141 pallets and a lorry delivered 50 more. Every pallet carries 9 cases. Each case holds 4 cartons, and every carton contains 6 sachets. A courier then dropped off 8 loose sachets at the office. The plant has been running for a dozen years. How many sachets are at the plant?
w10_T4_002287: Sofia had 37 jars of chutney on her stall and her mother brought 49 more from the kitchen. A neighbour added 27 jars of his own to the same table. Then 2 jars were knocked off and broken. Every jar on the table holds 8 spoonfuls of chutney. Her friend Marta, who had made fewer jars than Sofia, prepared twice as many spoonfuls as were on Sofia's table for the village hall tasting. How many spoonfuls did Marta prepare?
w10_T4_002288: On Friday morning Emeka had 104 trays of seedlings and sold 42 of them at the gate. Every tray still on his bench holds 8 seedlings. During the afternoon a landscaper planted 384 of those seedlings in a new park. In the evening his colleague Rosa, who grows far fewer seedlings than Emeka, took 40 more for her own borders. Emeka has raised seedlings here for a dozen years. How many seedlings are left on the bench?
